before.label: Failure domain
before.definition: A set of components that can fail together from a shared cause, such as a rack, power feed, switch, or software release.

changes.rationale: The documented domain groups machines by shared power and network dependencies. A domain is not a failure event, and network topology alone does not establish all dependency boundaries. This terminology correction does not approve the deferred safety-method relationships.

sources.supports: The documented domain groups machines by shared power and network dependencies. A domain is not a failure event, and network topology alone does not establish all dependency boundaries.

before.label: Functional insufficiency (SOTIF)
before.definition: Hazardous behavior arising without any fault, from limits of a specification or of a component's performance, such as perception errors under particular triggering conditions.

fields.label: Functional insufficiency
fields.definition: An insufficiency in the specification or performance of an intended function that can contribute to hazardous behavior without a fault covered by functional-safety analysis.

changes.rationale: SOTIF denotes the safety property, while a functional insufficiency is a specification or performance deficiency contributing to a hazard. The names are not equivalent. This terminology correction does not approve the deferred safety-method relationships.

sources.locator: ISO 21448:2022 catalog abstract (not the full normative text) (inspected 2026-11-04)

before.conditions: Components behind a shared switch, rack, or power feed fail together, so the topology fixes the failure domains.

fields.conditions: Components depend on shared network elements; power, software, and other dependencies may define additional or overlapping failure domains.
